information.description:
If you’ve ever heard someone make a passing remark about “‘saka cyberninjas,’ these flashes of death are what they were likely referring to. Trained in secret bases in Japan by masters of stealth and CQC, and outfitted with some of the best gear around, these Special Agents are used by the corporation for all manner of assignments that require discretion, precision, and speed. Basically, they’re mega-assassins.

From Corgo's 77 Collection: Mooks by Corgopolis (Arasaka).
information.notes:
Threat level: Elite Hardened Mini-Boss
Facedown #: 7
COM#: 14

Weapons:

  • Kendachi Mono-Three: ROF 1, 4d6. EQ; Ignores armor below SP11. Requires a valid Biometric Key.

Armor:

  • Light Armorjack (Body): SP 12 as printed (the item is SP 11); Tech Upgrade
  • Melee SP (head/body): 6/6

Situational skill values:

  • Melee Weapon 14 (15/16)
  • Perception 10 (12)

Not built:

  • Self-ICE x2 (in Neural Link): from official Cyberpunk RED material by R. Talsorian Games; not in the Cyberpunk RED - Core Foundry system

description.value: Experts in combat who use their fighting prowess to dominate in the lawless time of the Red.
An Exotic, Excellent Quality, Two-Handed Very Heavy Melee Weapon. It appears as a high-tech katana, able to ignore any armor below SP11.

Cost: 5,000eb (Luxury)

An Arasaka design meant for in-corp use, this ultra-light reinforced helm is equipped with advanced prediction software that scans targets, syncs with ‘saka data servers to predict enemy actions, and feeds this directly back to the HUD. In essence, a Neo-Kabuto lets a skilled bladedancer move like they see the future — because they can.

Despite denials by Arasaka, rumors persist of a secretive ‘Kagami’ model with improved optics, carbo-titanium armor, boosted software, and smartlink disruption tech, but those are just rumors, right?

SP 12 Head Armor with no Armor Penalty. Comes with built-in TUp (+1 Slot) Smart Glasses (w/ Anti-Dazzle & Low Light/Infrared/UV). While worn by a user with Melee Weapon Skill Level 7 or higher, or Combat Awareness Rank 2 or higher, this helmet’s custom software provides a +1 bonus to Melee Weapon Attack Checks, or a +2 bonus when making an Aimed Shot. This armor repairs itself for 1 point of lost SP at the end of each day in which it does not lose SP.

Covers: Head
SP: 12
Armor Penalty: none

Foundry notes:

  • The +1 is automated while equipped; add the extra point on Aimed Shots by hand, and disable the effect if you don't qualify.

From Corgo's 77 Collection V3 by Corgopolis (Armor & Fashion > Armor Catalog).
Light version of an Armorjack. No armor penalty.
Provides +2 to perception checks that use hearing.
A cybernetical replacement leg. Comes with a free foot.
Provides traction for climbing vertically. Must be paired.
Built-in hydraulics negates penalty for jumping. Must be paired.
A cybernetical replacement leg. Comes with a free foot.
Provides traction for climbing vertically. Must be paired.
Built-in hydraulics negates penalty for jumping. Must be paired.
Deals no damage. If hit roll DV15 Resist Torture/Drugs. On a fail take the Damaged Eye and Damaged Ear Critical injuries (see pg. 188) for 1 minute. No Crit damage dealt.

Cost: 1,000eb (Very Expensive) ♦ Install: Clinic

Humanity Loss: 7 (2d6)

Improves speed in melee combat via installing microscopic rotors at specific joint locations. Users with arthritis or weak bodies are advised to not install this cyberware without consulting a licensed ripperdoc.

Internal Body Cyberware. Requires 2 Option Slots. The user can activate this cyberare with an Action, after which it remains active for the next 6 seconds (2 Rounds). While active, ROF 1 Melee Weapons wielded in two hands or installed in a Cyberlimb/Battleglove function at ROF 2, and ROF 2 Melee Weapons (Before ROF increase) wielded in two hands or installed in a Cyberlimb/Battleglove can now make Aimed Shots at ROF 2. This cyberware has a 30 second (10 Rounds) cooldown before it can be activated again.

Type: Internal Body Cyberware
Install: Clinic
Option Slots: uses 2

Foundry notes:

  • The ROF change isn't automated; edit the weapon's ROF while this is active.

From Corgo's 77 Collection V3 by Corgopolis (Cyberware > Internal Body Cyberware).

Cost: 500eb (Expensive) ♦ Install: Hospital

Humanity Loss: 14 (4d6)

The modern Kerenzikov takes the place of the now defunct Reflex Co-Processor to help reduce the strain on the user's Neuroport.

Neuralware. The user can now dodge Ranged Attacks if they could not do so already, and gain a +2 bonus to Checks for noticing Ambushes.

NOTE: Credit to Infernox_Ratchet for the basis of this item.

Type: Neuralware
Install: Hospital
Option Slots: uses 1

Foundry notes:

  • Replaces the core system's Kerenzikov; use this one instead of the core item.
  • The +2 is on Perception and situational, because it only applies to noticing an Ambush: tick it in the roll dialog.

From Corgo's 77 Collection V3 by Corgopolis (Cyberware > Neuralware).

Cost: 500eb (Expensive)

If you want to stay in the game, you’re going to need a boost.

Kerenzikov Cyberware Enhancement. The Kerenzikov now counts as Speedware and also provides a +2 bonus to initiative at all times. Only 1 piece of Speedware can be installed at a time.

Enhances: Kerenzikov
Option Slots: 0 (Cyberware Enhancement)

Foundry notes:

  • The +2 initiative isn't automated from an upgrade; add it to the Kerenzikov as an Active Effect (bonuses.initiative) or apply it by hand.

From Corgo's 77 Collection V3 by Corgopolis (Cyberware > Neuralware).
